label: copy phase, step right after w was fed back (weak diffuse copy-phase background)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.8% of activation mass; essentially zero during original input and at <DEL>), and almost only on repeated tokens (in_first=0). The clearest part is the copy step right after w was input: precision about 0.76 there, and it holds 53% of the top activation quartile. Beyond that it fires weakly and diffusely across copy steps. It is somewhat more likely after e, u, or n, at recall_idx 2 (two steps after <DEL>), when the output is p, and in longer sequences, but none of these make a clean predicate. Adding prev e/u/n, out p, or early recall_idx kept F1 at about 0.41-0.46. The predicate misses roughly 56% of activation mass, mostly the low-magnitude background on other copy steps. It does not fire during the original phase, does not depend on digit count, and does not track copy correctness.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: w, e, u, n, c, z; least: a, 3, i, p) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: p, 1, r, u; delimiter step: u, f, c, n; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, recall_idx=2, phase=2.
